chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who led a group in prayer, so he prayed one rak'ah with them, then died. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They should bring forward another man, and they should count the rak'ah, and they should place the deceased behind them, and whoever touches him must perform ghusl.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for the congregation if the Imam dies during prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the procedural continuity of congregational prayer (Salat) when the Imam passes away mid-prayer, emphasizing the validity of the partial prayer and the specific ritual status of the deceased Imam. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the Imam's death does not invalidate the prayer but requires the congregation to appoint a successor, while also establishing the rule that touching the Imam's body necessitates ghusl, distinguishing his status from a regular deceased person. This ruling underscores the importance of maintaining the unity and continuity of the prayer unit (jamāʿah) even in the event of the leader's sudden death.
